messages:
Maya: quick heads-up — since the policy flip at 07:14 UTC, we're seeing a surge of 429s reported by multiple customers. Tickets from Acme and Orbital both show repeated 429 + increased latency. Putting this here to coordinate rollback if needed. :warning:

Owen: copying logs — I can see a spike in 429s starting 07:15:12 UTC from our edge cluster in us-west-2. 5xxs are low, but errors are overwhelmingly 429. Taking a sample:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RW-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RW-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RW-RateLimit-Reset: 164
X-RW-Quota-Window: monthly
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"requests per minute exceeded"}
```

Owen: headers show the new policy's burst window is smaller than the traffic tails expected by a few customers — looks like the staged flip reduced the per-client burst allowance by ~60% for some tiers. The flip was applied as a staged traffic change (15% -> 50% -> 100%). InfraBot: deployment event: "policy-flip rl/policy-v4-flip -> staged at 07:14 UTC to 20%".

Priya: thanks — we rolled rl/policy-v4-flip to 20% as an automated staged rollout this morning. Our canary metrics showed lower latency but we didn't surface per-customer burst tail behavior in SLO tests. Running quick diff vs policy-v3: burst_tokens=40 -> 16 for quota-tier:standard. That'll break clients that rely on short high-throughput bursts.

Jordan: customer impact note — Acme uses short-burst batch ingestion on a cron every 5m, so they suddenly hit 429 mid-batch and their ingestion job retries which drives more traffic. They're asking for immediate mitigation and a postmortem.

Maya: for triage, can someone post a reproducible curl sample I can drop into support tickets? Prefer one showing the headers customers see.

Owen: sure — here's an easy repro hitting the edge gateway with a token from a test acct:

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer TEST_TOKEN_X" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt": "x"}'
```

Then look for X-RW-RateLimit-* headers. If Remaining==0 and you get 429 body then it's the rate policy. Also check our internal proxy logs: `/var/log/proxy/edge-us-west2.log` has the client ip and token hash.

Priya: recommended immediate actions: 1) pause the staged flip (stop ramp to 100%), 2) rollback to rl/policy-v3 for the affected traffic slice, 3) add short-term exemption for customers with known ingestion patterns while we tune policy-v4. We should avoid a full org-wide rollback until we've verified metrics.

Owen: I can run the rollback for the 20% slice now. Command I’ll run: `infractl policy rollback --policy rl/policy-v4-flip --target-slice 20% --to rl/policy-v3` (this is the internal operation). ETA ~3-4m to see effect in edge metrics.

Maya: I'll notify Acme and Orbital that we're pausing the new limits and working on remediation. Jordan, can you draft a short status update we can paste in tickets?

Jordan: on it. Draft: "We're aware of intermittent 429s after a rate policy update and have paused the rollout. Our engineering team is rolling affected traffic back to the prior policy; you may see transient 429s clear within a few minutes. We're investigating permanent fixes and will follow up with a timeline for a tuned rollout." Anything to add?

Maya: include a quick repro snippet and the header explanation. Also ask them to share request patterns if they can (timestamps + client ids).

InfraBot: policy rollout action queued: rollback rl/policy-v4-flip -> rl/policy-v3 for slice 20%. initiated_by: owen. action_id: act-20260315-019.

Owen: running now. watching metrics.

[~3m later]

Owen: rollback applied. I've verified proxy metrics showing 429 rate drop by ~72% for the affected tenant buckets. Latency also normalized.

Maya: reporting back to customers now. Jordan, attach the sample curl, and note that we've reverted the staged change.

Jordan: update posted to Acme and Orbital tickets. Also flagged to their CSMs.

Priya: post-incident follow-ups: 1) create a short test harness that simulates short-burst ingestion patterns (cron-batch) and include in our canary suite; 2) revert policy-v4 baseline to use burst_tokens=32 for quota-tier:standard and rerun A/B; 3) add an automated alert that checks per-customer 429 tail spikes during staged rollouts. I'll open tickets for these.

Owen: agree. I'll paste a small log snippet for the postmortem showing before/after counts, and attach the infractl command history. Also recommending a two-step staged rollout for future flips: first functional perf checks at 10% for 30m including per-tenant tail tests, then ramp.

Maya: quick note on billing/auth — no billing changes detected and tokens are valid; this was purely rate-policy behavior. Good to confirm.

Jordan: closing loop: customers are seeing successful retries clear after rollback, and both customers acknowledged the update. They asked for ETA on the tuned rollout; we'll provide once Priya's team has a validated patch and extra canary checks.

Maya: thanks everyone. Action items assigned: Priya -> canary harness + policy tweak ticket, Owen -> infra rollback logs + monitoring rule, Jordan -> customer comms + follow-up, Maya -> collect tickets and close. Marking resolved for now until postmortem. :white_check_mark:
